en: *Kṛdantarūpamālā*, entry for *aka* (1): “*aka* [is used] in the sense of crooked motion” (I-bhvādiḥ-792, transitive, seṭ, parasmaipadī); it belongs to the *ghaṭādi* group and is marked as *mit*. Regarding this, Deva states in verse 41: “The root *tvaṅk* is derived from *idit* [roots]; there, *aka* is used in the sense of crooked motion. With the suffixes *ṇic*, *san*, *ṇvul*, and *āka*: *ākakaḥ*—*kikā*; *akakaḥ*—*kikā*; *acikiṣakaḥ*—*ṣikā*.
The feminine forms of the agentive suffix *tṛn* (*tṛ*) are: *akitā-trī*, *akayitā-trī*, *acikiṣitā-trī*;
the present participles are *akan-ntī*, *akayan-ntī*, *acikiṣan-ntī*;
and the future participles are *akiṣyan-ntī-tī*, *akayiṣyan-ntī-ntī*, *acikiṣiṣyan-ntī-tī*.
The present participle middle: *akayamānaḥ*, *akayiṣyamāṇaḥ*;
with the suffix *kvip*: *ak-akau*, *akaḥ*; the past passive participle (*niṣṭhā*): *akitam* (or *ātaḥ*), *akitaḥ*, *acikiṣitaḥ*, *tam*, *tavān*.
Other suffixes (*pratyaya*) beginning with *ak*: *akaḥ*, *akaḥ*; [desiderative] *acikīṣuḥ*, *acikayiṣuḥ*;
[gerundive] *tavya*: *akitavyam*, *akayitavyam*, *acikīṣitavyam*; [gerundive in] *-anīya*: *akanīyam*, *akanīyam*, *acikīṣaṇīyam*.
The suffixes *ṇyat* or *yat*: *ākyam*, *akyam*, *acikīṣyam*; the suffix *khal*: *īṣadakaḥ*, *durakaḥ*, *svakaḥ*;
the suffix *yak*: *ākyamānaḥ*, *akyamānaḥ*, *acikīṣyamāṇaḥ*.
The *ghañ* suffixes: *ākaḥ*, *akaḥ*, *acikiṣaḥ*; the *tumun* suffixes: *akitum*, *akayitum*, *acikiṣitum*;
the *ktin* suffixes: *aktiḥ*, *akanā*, *acikiṣā*, *acikayiṣā*.
The suffix *lyuṭ*: *akanam*, *akayanam*, *acikīṣaṇam*; the suffix *ktvā*: *akitvā*, *akayitvā*, *acikīṣitvā*;
the suffix *lyap*: *samakya*, *samakayya*, *samacikīṣya*.
Note: *ktvā* and *ṇamul* are not *akit*; [the forms are] *ākam-ākam*, *ākam-ākam*, *akam-akam*, *akam-akam*, *akayitvā-akayitvā*, *acikiṣam-acikiṣam*; *acikiṣitvā-acikiṣitvā*.

*āgakaḥ* / *-gikā*, *agakaḥ* / *-gikā*, *ajigiṣakaḥ* / *-ṣikā*; and so forth.
Everything should be understood as being like the [root] *aghāt* (1).

[5 0006] Regarding *aghi*: (6) “*aghi* in the sense of motion and incitement” (*bhvādi*-class, I-109, transitive, *seṭ*, root-final vowel *ā*). Motion and incitement (*gatyākṣepa*) means censure (*nindā*), as well as motion and the commencement of motion.
Forms such as *aṅghakaḥ* / *aṅghikā*, *añjighiṣakaḥ* / *añjighiṣikā*, and so forth, derive from the root *aki* in the sense of “marking” (*lakṣaṇe*).

Because the root is invariably accompanied by the causative suffix (*ṇic*), forms devoid of *ṇic* do not occur. Furthermore, because it contains more than one vowel (*anekāc*), forms belonging to the intensive (*yaṅ*) are also absent.

Aja (9): "aja" [in the senses of] "motion" and "throwing" (bhvādi, I-230, sakarmaka, seṭ, parasmaipada); "throwing" means "impelling."

In the absence of the *ṅit* designation, after the application of *guṇa* and *ādeśa*, the form is *ūrṇunaviṣakaḥ*. In the case where it has the *ṅit* designation, with the substitution of *uvaṅ*, the form is *ūrṇunuviṣakaḥ*. Thus, that which ends in *īyaṅ* possesses the status of a verbal root (*dhātu*). From this, suffixes such as *ṇvul* follow. The root *kakhe* means "to laugh" (*hasane*). It belongs to the first class (*bhvādi*), number 784; it is intransitive (*akarmaka*), takes the *seṭ* suffix, is parasmaipada, and belongs to the *ghaṭādi* subgroup.
The derivative forms include: *kākhakaḥ* / *khikā*, *cikakhiṣakaḥ* / *ṣikā*, *cākakhakaḥ* / *khikā*, and so forth.

The forms of *kakh* should be understood sequentially from the root in its pure (*śuddha*) state, from the present participle (*sannanta*), and from the intensive (*yaṅanta*), just like the previously mentioned root *kakha* (141). However, in the causative (*ṇyanta*), because it is listed among the *ghaṭādi* roots, the rule "ghaṭādayo mitaḥ" (Gaṇasūtra, Bhvādi class) applies the designation *mit*; consequently, by the rule "mitāṃ hrasvaḥ" (Pāṇini 6.4.92), the vowel is shortened, resulting in these forms: *kakhakaḥ*, *khikā*, *kakhyamānaḥ*.

Some say that this means its specific meaning is not stated because it has the general sense of action (*kriyāsāmānyārthatvāt*). It belongs to the *bhvādi* class (number 791), is intransitive (*akarmaka*), takes the suffix *seṭ*, is parasmaipada, and belongs to the *ghaṭādi* subgroup.

Others say that because it has multiple meanings, all the forms of this root— whether from the simple form, the *sa*-present (*sannanta*), or the intensive (*yaṅanta*)— should be understood to be like those of the root *kakh* (141). However, when derived from the causative (*ṇyant*), they should be understood like the roots of the *ghaṭādi* class, such as "kakhe hasane" (142).

(176–177) The root *kalla*, meaning "inarticulate sound," belongs to the first class (*bhvādi*), number 498; it is intransitive (*akarmaka*), takes the *seṭ* augment, and is used in the middle voice (*ātmanepada*).

Regarding the statement “*kattha* [is used] in the sense of praise” (160), all its forms are to be understood as being like those of the root belonging to the *bhūvādika* class. Kṣīrasvāmin and others read this root as *kalla* in the sense of “not sounding” (*aśabda*).
They further explain that “not sounding” means “silence” (*tūṣṇīmbhāva*).

Regarding this, Deva states in verse 67: "One should use *guñjet* for an indistinct sound; one should use *gujet* for sound in general."

Some read the root as *guj*. In the case where it is marked with the *it* augment (*idit*), the forms are *guñjakaḥ* / *guñjikā*, *guñjakaḥ* / *guñjikā*, *juguñjiṣakaḥ* / *juguñjiṣikā*, *joguñjakaḥ* / *joguñjikā*, *guñjan* / *guñjatī*, *guñjā*; these and other such forms are to be understood as being like those of *kuṇṭh* (209). In the case where it is not marked with the *it* augment (*anidit*), the forms are *gojakaḥ* / *gojikā*, and so forth.

[470 0457] The root *ghuṣir* (471), meaning "to make a sound" (*viśabdane*), belongs to the *curādi* class (No. 1727). It is *akarmaka*, *seṭ*, and *ubhayapadī* [a]. [The rule states: "In the case of *ghuṣ*, when preceded by a causative suffix (*ṇic*) and meaning 'to make a sound,' [the *iṭ* augment is prohibited]; however, it is not so when it does not mean 'to make a sound.'"
"From *ghoṣati* it is derived *ghuṃṣet*; *ghuṃṣate* is used in the sense of the act of beautifying," says the Lord [Patañjali].

The causative suffix (*ṇic*) for this root is optional. For this very reason, in the rule "ghuṣir aviśabdane" (Aṣṭādhyāyī 7.2.23), the term "not in the sense of sound" (*aviśabdane*) is employed to prevent the prohibition of the augment *iṭ* in the past passive participle (*niṣṭhā*) of this root.

The word [aviśabdane] would be redundant if this root were invariably followed by the causative suffix (*ṇij*) because, in that case, the prohibition [of *iṇ*] would already be established due to the absence of the *niṣṭhā* suffix immediately following the root. Therefore, the causative suffix (*ṇic*) is optional.

Thus, on the view where the causative suffix is absent, that word becomes meaningful for the purpose of preventing the prohibition of *iṇ*; in this way, it achieves its own intended purpose (*svāṃśe cāritārthyam*).

Since the suffix *ṇic* is optional, all forms—just like those of the root *ghuṣi* (470)—should be understood from the pure root (*śuddha-dhātu*), from the root with the desiderative suffix (*sannanta*), and from the root with the intensive suffix (*yaṅanta*) of the *bhūvādigaṇa*. However, when the *niṣṭhā* suffix follows, only "saṃghuṣitaṃ vākyam" is correct. These forms are now written out from the causative (*ṇyanta*) and from the desiderative derived from that causative base.

→1. Having introduced the governing rule *ārdhadhātuke* (Pāṇini 2.4.35), the substitution of *khyāñ* for the root *cakṣiṅ* is prescribed by the rule *cakṣiṅaḥ khyāñ* (2.4.54). The author of the Bhāṣya maintains that this substitute begins with *khś* (i.e., *khśāñ*), and he accepts the statement *śasya yo vā* (Vārttika 8.4.39) immediately after the section on the substitution of *ṇ* in the *asiddha* portion of the grammar. Consequently, the substitution of *y* (*yatva*) is optional. In the case where *y* is substituted, the form *khyāpayati* arises through the addition of the augment *yuk* by the rule *āto yuk ciṇ-kṛtoḥ* (7.3.33). In the alternative case where *y* is not substituted, the *kh* of *khś* becomes *k* by the rule *khari ca* (8.4.55), resulting in the form *kśāyakaḥ*.
In this manner, two forms are to be understood everywhere in the case of *ārdhadhātuka* suffixes.

→ 2. The augment *puk* occurs when the suffix ends in *ā*. This should be understood to apply everywhere in the case of causative (*ṇyanta*) forms. → 3.

The rule *ciṇṇamuloḥ* (Pāṇini 6.4.93) does not apply here because, due to the inclusion of this root among those ending in long vowels (*adanta*), the elision of the penultimate vowel (*allop*) acts as a *sthānivadbhāva* (as if it were still present), creating an intervention; furthermore, since the condition of being followed by a *ṇit* suffix is absent, the rule *ata upadhāyāḥ* (Pāṇini 7.2.116) does not cause the *vṛddhi* strengthening. → [a] The root *chadir-ūrjane* is listed among the *bhvādi* roots. In that context, *chadi-* is indicated with a short *i*.

*Ūrjanam* means strengthening or giving life. Since the root *chad-* listed among the *curādi* roots is optional in its causative suffix (*ṇic*) because it belongs to the *ādhṛṣīya* group, this is a re-statement for the sake of establishing the *mit* designation in the alternative case where the *ṇic* is absent in its own sense. Because roots have multiple meanings, it functions here in the sense of "strengthening. To employ a form ending in *chad* is expressed as *chadayati*, meaning "he makes strong" or "he gives life."

But when it is used in its own sense (*svārthe*) as a causative (*ṇyanta*) meaning "to cover" (*chādayati*), then it becomes strong (*balībhavati*), or "to become vital" (*prāṇībhavati*), or the meaning is "to ward off" (*apavārayati*). In that case, because of the rule "other [roots] are not *mit* when there is no *hetu*" (Gaṇasūtra under the *curādi* class), the *mit* designation does not apply. The reading "in the sense of covering and straightening" (*chadir-arjane*) seen in some places is not traditional. [The root is] "cheda in the sense of warding off" (*apavāraṇe*).

Thus, it is understood that even for the root *chada* occurring later in the *curādi* [class], the reading *chada* alone—though accepted by Kṣīrasvāmin—is non-Vedic (*anārṣa*). Both Deva and Puruṣakāra also support the meaning stated by us.
Furthermore, rules such as *chāder ghe 'dvyupasargasya* (Pāṇini 6.4.96) would otherwise be impossible if this root were not included among the *bhvādi* roots.

It should also be understood that [the form] *gamakāni* is derived as follows: 1. From the root *gam*, with the suffix *ṇic* added in its own sense (*svārthe*), the form is produced by the rule *ata upadhāyāḥ* (Pāṇini 7.2.116), which effects the vṛddhi strengthening of the penultimate vowel.

By the rule *ścuḥ* (Pāṇini 8.4.40), the letter *c* is substituted [for *ch*]. This should be understood to apply likewise in the case of the suffix *saN* and the suffix *yaṅ*. 3. Consequently, in the alternative where *ṇic* is absent, the form is derived from the root alone with the suffix *ṇvul*. This is because, according to the principle *jñāpakasiddhaṃ na sarvatra* (Paribhāṣā 126)—"that which is established by an indicator [of grammatical usage] does not apply everywhere"—its inclusion is nonetheless secured. From the root *jṛ* (to grow old), the forms *jarakaḥ*, *jarayan*, *jarā*, *jarītvā*/*jaritvā*, and *jaram* (or *jāram*) occur, among others. However, from the root *jṛṇāti*, the forms *jārakaḥ*, *jārayan*, *jīrṇiḥ*, *jarītvā*/*jaritvā*, and *jāram* (or *jāram*) occur; this is the distinction.

Because *jārayati* belongs to the *ādhṛṣīya* group beginning with *caurādi*, in the absence of the causative suffix (*ṇic*), all its forms are like those of a root belonging to the *krayādi* group; however, there is a distinction in the present participle (*śatṛ*), which is *jaraṃ*. In the *Mādhavīyadhātuvṛtti*, it is stated that after a thorough examination of the *Bhāṣya*, the *Vārttika*, the *Vṛtti*, the *Nyāsa*, the *Padamañjarī*, and other works, the inclusion of *jṛṇāti* [in the *bhūvādigaṇa*] is unauthoritative. Since the supporting texts such as the *Vṛtti* and *Nyāsa* are not available, let the wise determine the truth of the matter here.

Let them decide. Regarding the statement in the *Uddyota* on the Vārttika "dārajārau kartari, ṇiluk ca" (3.3.20): "But surely the root *jṛ* is also listed in the *kryādi* group; for this very reason, the letter *ṣ* was pronounced in the Gaṇasūtra 'janījṝṣ-' (in the *bhvādi* group) in order to exclude that [root]. And since that [root] is *mit*, the form *jārayati* would be established from it even by the elision of *ṇi* when the suffix *ghañ* is applied. If this is objected, [the answer is: no, because [the *ṣ*] is for the purpose of excluding the form *jaraḥ* [which would otherwise result] from a *mit* root."

Here, the meaning of the root listed in the *ghaṭādi* group is both *nṛtya* (acting) and *nṛtta* (dancing). *Nṛtya* is the mimetic representation of the meaning of words (*padārthābhinaya*). *Nṛtta* is the movement of the limbs devoid of such representation, consisting of the flexion of body parts as prescribed by the treatises (*śāstra*), for which those who perform it are commonly designated as *nartaka* (dancers).

In these two senses, the grammatical operation conditioned by *mit*-status applies; likewise, the status of being a *ṇopadeśa* applies only in this sense. However, in the sense of "trembling" (*avaspandana*), there is no *mit*-status.

According to the *Ṇopadeśakārikā*, by the formulation containing the long vowel in the rule "aṇāṭi," the status of being a *ṇopadeśa* is prohibited for that which is eligible for lengthening. Kṣīrasvāmī, however, having read [the root] as "natau," states "naṭayati."

Having cited "śākhām," he stated: "In the sense of *nṛt* (dancing), however, [the root] is used as *naṭati* and *nāṭayati*. (1-2-4) Thus, there is the status of being treated as having the marker *ṅ* (*ṅidvadbhāva*). By means of that, the form [is established] through processes such as *samprasāraṇa*. The same procedure should be understood for the suffix *śānac* as well.

→ 3. In the case of the *kvip* suffix: when the initial consonant of a *saṃyoga* cluster is elided due to its position at the end of a word (*padāntanimittaka*), followed by *samprasāraṇa*, the substitution of *ṣ* for the letter *j*, and the substitutions of *jaśtva* and *cartva*.

The form *rūpam* is thus. *Dhānābhṛṭ* means "a frying pan. This word is cited in the *Kāśikā* on Pāṇini 8.2.36. The statement "on account of the indicative mark" (tilliṅgāt) is indicated. Its meaning is as follows: in a context where a semivowel is subject to vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*), the application of the rule *bhrasjo ropadhayo ram anyatarasyām* (Pāṇini 6.4.47) does not occur; the reason for this is the indicative mark (*liṅga*) consisting of the mention of the word *bhṛṣṭaluñcita* in the *rājadantādi* group (Pāṇini 2.2.31).

However, in the *Gaṇaratnamahodadhi*, within the *rājadantādi* group (pp. 120–121), it is stated: "First *luñcitam* = removed, afterwards *bhṛṣṭam* = cooked; thus *bhṛṣṭaluñcitam*. For example: 'The moon-dish, whose rabbit was first cooked and then plucked out. This point should be noted here.

→ 1. From a *yaṅ*-intensive base, by adding the suffix *ac* [via Pāṇini 3.1.134], and then by the elision of *yaṅ* [via Pāṇini 2.4.74], since the elision (*luk*) is a cause for prohibiting the status of being "as if present" (*sthānivadbhāva*), the *ṅit*-ness caused by *yaṅ* is not relied upon; therefore, processes such as *saṃprasāraṇa* do not occur. Furthermore, because there is no subsequent *ārddhadhātuka* suffix, the addition of the augment *ram*, the removal of the penultimate vowel *r*, and so forth, also do not occur. Consequently, in this case:

According to the grammatical treatise (*śāstra*), in the case of repetition (*abhyāsa*), there is lengthening by the rule "dīrgho'kitaḥ" (Pāṇini 7.4.83). It should be understood that in the subsequent portion (*uttarakhaṇḍa*), the substitution of *ś* for *s* (*ścutva*) and the substitution of the voiced unaspirated stop (*jaśtva*) occur. Regarding this root: because it is *aniṭ* (lacking the *iṭ* augment) in the past participle (*niṣṭhā*), when the suffix *ṇyat* is applied, there is the removal of the penultimate vowel (*ropadhani-vṛtti*) in the alternative where the augment *ram* is not added; then, by the rule "cajoḥ ku ghiṇṇyatoḥ" (Pāṇini 7.3.52), the *j* is changed to *k*, resulting in the form *bhargyam*. However, in the alternative where the augment *ram* and others do not occur, the rule "pūrvatrāsiddham" (Pāṇini 8.2.1) dictates that the change to *k* occurs before the change to the voiced unaspirated stop (*jaśtva*).

Thus, after the *kutva* [change of *bhram* to *bhrām*] has occurred, and subsequently the *sakāra* is changed to *dakāra* by the rule for *jaśtva*, it should be understood that the form is *bhradgyam*. In the same way, one should understand the cause for the derivation of these two forms even when the suffix *ghañ* is applied.

→ 3. When the suffix *lyap* is applied, because it is treated as having the status of the original (*sthānivadbhāva*), the semivowel undergoes *samprasāraṇa*, and the *sakāra* undergoes *ścutva*; thus the form is established in this manner.

→1. *bhrājṛ* (1187), "ṭu bhrājṛ dīptau" (I-bhvādiḥ-181. 823, aka., seṭ, ātmanepada): *bhrājakaḥ* / *-jikā*, *bhrājakaḥ* / *-jikā*, *bibhrājiṣakaḥ* / *-ṣikā*, *bābhrājakaḥ* / *-jikā*;

These are the forms that occur for this root; this is the distinction. In the first section of the *Bhvādi* class, having listed "bhrājṛ dīptau" (to shine), it is listed again in the *Ghaṭādi* class as "ṭu bhrājṛ".

The root is read as *dīptau* ("in the sense of shining"). Thus, it is understood that both of these [roots, *bhrāj* and *dīp*] have the meaning "to shine" and are marked with the *ṛt* indicatory letter (*ṛdit*).
However, the author of the Nyāsa read only *bhrāja dīptau* in the rule *bhrājabhāsadhurvi-* (Pāṇini 3.2.177). In the Padamañjarī as well (on 7.4.3), the reading appears to be only *bhrāja dīptau*.

"The inclusion of the marker *ṛt* in the root *bhrāj* is un-Pāṇinian"—this is to be understood from the *Kāśikā* on 7.4.3. The *Mādhavīyā Dhātuvṛtti* states: "The status of being marked with *ṛt* has as its sole result [the designation] *anudāttet*. Since the status of being marked with *ṛt* is useful only in the context of verbal endings (*tiṅanta*), we have included both roots together. Among the *ghaṭādi* group, the *phaṇādi* roots are included.

The seven roots are listed at the end [of the section]. Among them, the reading is simply “*ṭu bhrājṛ*,” which is the consensus of Ttyāsakāra, Maitreyarakṣita, Puruṣakāra, Sāyaṇa, the *Siddhāntakaumudī*, and others. Kṣīrasvāmī, however, having read “*bhrājṛ, ṭu bhrāśṛ,*” etc., says: “Some say that *ṭu* applies to both [roots]. From ‘*ṭvito'thuc*’ (Pāṇini 3.3.89), we have *bhrājathuḥ*. In the *dhātupāṭha* of the Cāndras and the Kāśakṛtsnīyas, only “*bhrāja*” is read in the *ghaṭādi* group, and not “*ṭu bhrājṛ*,” as noted in the commentary on Kṣīrataraṅgiṇī.

This has been explained; all of this should be considered here. Although the statement of the author of the *Nyāsa*—“Since forms such as *bhrājate* are established by means of [the suffixes] *phaṇ* and so on, which must necessarily be recited, their inclusion here (i.e., among the *bhū*-class roots distinct from *ghaṭ* etc. is as if it were not of the original seers (*anārṣa*)”—is cited in the *Mādhavīya Dhātuvṛtti*, it should also be taken into account here.
→ 1. By the rule “*bhrājabhāsadhurvi-*” (Pāṇini 3.2.177), the suffix *kvip* is applied to form agent nouns denoting those who possess such a habit (*tacchīla*) and so forth.

By the rule “*coḥ kuḥ*” (8.2.30), the substitution of *k* occurs at the end of a word (*padānte*). It should be understood that this is the form of the root *bhrāj* (meaning "to shine") belonging to the *bhūvādigaṇa*, which is listed among the *ghaṭādi* roots as *bhrājṛ dīptau*.
→1. “It was adorned by those who were radiant, unvanquished, and never grieved by any living being whatsoever. (*Dhātukāvya* 1.25). →2.

Regarding the rule *bhuvaśca* (Pāṇini 3.2.138), the *Kāśikā* and other works state that by the word *ca* (“and”), the suffix *iṇnuc* is also applied to this root (*bhū*). In this regard as well, many hold that the form *bhrājiṣṇu* is derived from both types of the root *bhrāj*.

Taking the *Kāśikā*’s example “*bhrājiṣṇunā lohitacandanena*” (‘with shining red sandalwood’), the *Padamañjarī* states: “This is not supported by the *Bhāṣya*. Now, in the *Bhāṣya* commentaries, [the rule] “*bhuvaśca*”...

We do not find the *Bhāṣya* on the rule (Pāṇini 3.2.138) at all. However, in the *Dhātukāvya-vyākhyāna* (2.20), it is explained that the suffix *iṣṇuc* is added to the root *bhrājṛ* of the *ghāṭādi* class:
"Kṛṣṇa also shone on the path, his sides illuminated by the radiant cowherd boys" (*Dhātukāvya* 2.20).

→ 3. From the root *bhrājṛ* with the suffix *kvip* in the sense of habitual action (*tācchīlika*), the substitution of *ṣ* occurs by the rule *vraścabhrasjasṛjamṛjayajarājabhrāja-* (Pāṇini 8.2.36), followed by the changes of *jaś*-ness and *cartva*-ness, resulting in this form. Although *vibhrāṭ* is cited as an example in the *Kāśikā* under the rule prescribing *kvip* (3.2.177), [this applies] to the two roots listed in the *Ghaṭādi* group within that sūtra.

In that case, both other roots [bhrāj] are indeed included; however, regarding the substitution of *ṣ* [for *s*], it is clear from the *Mādhavīya Dhātuvṛtti* on the present topic that, due to the association with the root *rāj* in the rule "vraścabhrasja— " (Pāṇini 8.2.36), this applies only to the *phaṇādi* (i.e., *ghaṭādi*) class of the root *bhrāj*.
→ 4. In the sense of an abstract action (*bhāva*), with the suffix *athuc* according to Pāṇini 3.3.89 (*ṭvito'thuc*), the form is thus.

However, for a root belonging to the *ghaṭādi* class, when followed by *kvasu*, there is an option regarding the substitution of *e* and the elision of the reduplication (*abhyāsa-lopa*) by the rule "phaṇāṃ ca saptānām" (Pāṇini 6.4.125). Consequently—
Two forms are to be known:

6. Regarding the form *bhrātā* [meaning] "one who shines," it appears in the *Kṣīrataraṅgiṇī* and in the *Daśapādya-ṇādīvṛtti* (2.3), derived from the root *bhrāj-* with the suffixes *tṛn* or *tṛc*, with the elision of *ja* by virtue of its belonging to the *pṛṣodarādi* group (Pāṇini 6.3.109).

And this has been established. However, in the Bhāṣya on [Pāṇini 1.2.68], since it is stated, "If he supports [others], he is a *bhrātṛ*," it appears that the derivation of the word *bhrātṛ* from the verbal root *bibharti* itself is more logical.

The state of *prakṛti* (original form).

[1187 0983] The root *bhrāśṛ* (1188), "to shine" (*ṭu bhrāśṛ dīptau*), belongs to the first class (*bhvādi*, no. 824), is intransitive (*akarmaka*), takes the *seṭ* augment, and is used in the middle voice (*ātmanepada*). As Deva states: "In the sense of shining, one says *bhrāśate*, *bhlāśate*; likewise, *bhrāśyate*, *bhlāśyate*. (Śloka 167).

*bhrāśakaḥ* / *bhrāśikā*, *bhrāśakaḥ* / *bhrāśikā*, *bibhrāśiṣakaḥ* / *bibhrāśiṣikā*, *bābhrāśakaḥ* / *bābhrāśikā*; all such forms are to be understood as being like those of the root *kāśati* belonging to the *bhūvādigaṇa* (No. 186). The distinction is that the forms *bhrāśyamānaḥ* and *bhrāśamānaḥ* are derived from the suffix *śānac*. [The form] *bhrāśathuḥ* [and] *bhrāśitaḥ*.
→ Regarding *śānac*, the suffix *śyan* is optionally applied by the rule “*vā bhrāśa-*” (Pāṇini 3.1.70).

*bhrī* (1189), “*bhrī* in the sense of fear” (IX, *kryādi*, 1505. transitive, intransitive, parasmaipada). It belongs to both the *pvādi* and *lvādi* groups. [The derivatives are: *bhrāyakaḥ*/*bhrāyikā*, *bhrāyakaḥ*/*bhrāyikā*, *bibhrīṣakaḥ*/*bibhrīṣikā*, *bebhrīyakaḥ*/*bebhrīyikā*.

*bhretā-trī*, *bhrāyayitā-trī*, *bibhrīṣitā-trī*, *bebhrīyitā-trī*; all such forms are to be understood like the root *plī* (1081) of the *kryādi* class. The specific differences are: *bhrīṇam-ṇaḥ-ṇavān*, *bhrītam-taḥ-tavān*, and *bhriṇan* (or *bhrintī*).
According to the commentary on the *Dhātukāvyā* (3.9): "This [root] also possesses the status of beginning with *lū*," as stated in the *Drume*.
Due to its inclusion in the *lvādi* group, by the rule *lvādibhyaḥ* (Pāṇini 8.2.44), the *niṣṭhā* suffix [takes the substitute *na*,] and the *nakāra* undergoes *ṇatva*, resulting in this form.

→ 4. In the present participle (*śatṛ*), the *vikaraṇa* suffix *śnā* is applied by the rule *kryādibhyaḥ* (3.1.81). By the rule *śnābhyastayor ātaḥ* (6.4.112), there is elision of the long *ā*, and by the rule *pvādīnāṃ hrasvaḥ* (7.3.80), the vowel is shortened.
And the form is thus when there is *ṇatva*:
"By the elephant, who possessed a body thick with pride, who was ignorant-minded, and who was pursued in order to seize [the prey]. — *Dhātukāvya* 3.9.
*bhrukṣa* (1190), meaning "to cover" (*saṃvaraṇe*), belongs to the *tudādi* class (VI), number 1395; it is *sakarmaka* (transitive), *seṭ* (having an *iṭ* augment), and follows the *kuṭādi* subgroup.

We include this root here according to the opinion of Maitreya and Kṣīrasvāmin. Although it is not listed in the *Siddhāntakaumudī* and other such works, nor in the *Mādhavīyā Dhātuvṛtti*, nevertheless, it appears in the *Mādhavīyā Dhātuvṛtti* within the section on the *cukṣa* roots.
It should also be understood that this is supported by the observation of agreement with the reading accepted by Maitreyarakṣita in the *tudādi* group.

All forms such as *bhrokṣakaḥ* / *-kṣikā*, *bhrokṣakaḥ* / *-kṣikā*, *bubhrukṣiṣakaḥ* / *-ṣikā*, and *bobhrukṣakaḥ* / *-kṣikā* should be understood to follow the pattern of *kuṭati* (Dhp. 204) in the *tudādi* class.

[1190 0985] *bhrūṇa* (1191). “*bhrūṇa* in the sense of hope” (Xth class, *curādi*-group, no. 1691; intransitive, with *iṭ*, middle voice). It belongs to the *ākusmīya* group. It is listed in the *dhātupāṭha* as “—in the sense of hope (*āśā*) and apprehension (*viśaṅkā*)”; [another version reads] “—in the sense of expectation (*āśaṃsā*)”.
Thus says Maitreya.

*Bhrūṇaka*, *bhrūṇikā*; *bubhrūṇayiṣaka*, *bubhrūṇayiṣikā*; *bhrūṇayitṛ*, *bhrūṇayitrī*; *bubhrūṇayiṣitṛ*, *bubhrūṇayiṣitrī*—all such forms are to be understood like those of the root *kūṭayati* from the curādigaṇa (240). [The word] *bhrūṇaḥ* [is derived with the suffix] *ā*.
→ ā. “Beholding the body of the embryo, with eyes half-closed and face slightly smiling, as it was about to produce deceit. Dhā. Kā. 3.35.

*bhrejṛ* (1192), meaning "to shine" (*dīptau*), belongs to the *bhū*-class (I-bhvādiḥ), number 180. It is *akarmaka* (intransitive), *seṭ* (having an *iṭ* augment), and *ātmanepada*. The forms are as follows: * Present active participle: *bhejakaḥ* / *bhejikā*; * Present middle participle: *bhejakaḥ* / *bhejikā*; * Desiderative active participle: *bibhrejiṣakaḥ* / *bibhrejiṣikā*; * Desiderative middle participle: *bebhrejiṣakaḥ* / *bebhrejiṣikā*; * Future active participle: *bhejitā* / *bhejitṛ*; * Future middle participle: *bhejayitā* / *bhejayitrī*; * Desiderative future active participle: *bibhrejiṣitā* / *bibhrejiṣitrī*; * Desiderative future middle participle: *bebhrejitā* / *bebhrejitṛ*. All such forms are to be understood as being like those of the root *kepat* (number 261) of the *bhū*-class. The specific distinction occurs in the *kvip* formation: *vibhrek*, *vibhreg*, *vibhrejau*, *vibhrejaḥ*. Thus ends the treatment.

[[1192 0986]] *Bhreṣṛ* (1193): “*Bhreṣṛ* in the sense of ‘going’” (I-bhvādiḥ-884. transitive, with *iṭ*, both [voices]). Bhaitreya states that it is also written as *bheṣṛ*. Kṣīrasvāmin read it as “in the sense of fear and movement. Others read it as *bhleṣṛ*; thus says the Dhātupradīpa (2.27).

*bhreṣakaḥ* / *bhreṣikā*, *bhreṣakaḥ* / *bhreṣikā*, *bibhreṣiṣakaḥ* / *bibhreṣiṣikā*, *bebhreṣakaḥ* / *bebhreṣikā*; *bhreṣitā* / *bhreṣitrī*, *bhreṣayitā* / *bhreṣayitrī*, *bibhreṣiṣitā* / *bibhreṣiṣitrī*, *bebhreṣitā* / *bebhreṣitrī*; all such forms are to be understood like those of the root *gepa-* (No. 429) of the *bhūvādi* class. Since this root is *ubhayapadin* (active and middle), [the forms] in the present participle (*śatṛ*)...
The forms *bhreṣantī*, *bhreṣiṣyantī* (and *bhreṣiṣyatī*), and so forth, are additional; this is the distinction.
→ *bh.* “The venerable one, who destroys the sin of those who look upon her with wandering eyes, like a fish [devouring] its prey... — Dhātukārikā 2.27.

*bhlakṣa* (1194): " *bhlakṣa* in the sense of eating" (I-bhvādiḥ-893. aka. seṭ. ubha.). Kṣīrasvāmī states " *bhakṣa*," as mentioned in the *Mādhavīya-dhātuvṛtti*; the same is stated in the *Puruṣakāra*. Maitreya says " *bhakṣa*"; Durga says " *plakṣa*. However, in the printed *Kṣīrataraṅgiṇī*, the reading " *bhlakṣa*" is indeed seen. Since Kṣīrasvāmī himself, under the root *bhakṣa* (21) in the *curādi* group, stated " *bhakṣateḥ ghañ* — *bhakṣaḥ*," and because there is no mention of a root *bhakṣati* meaning "eating" anywhere among the *bhvādi* roots, this very [root *bhlakṣ*] [is the one intended].
The root *bhā* is derived from the sense "he eats" (*bhakṣati*), thus it is called *bhāti*. However, Durga and others read this root as *plakṣa*.

This is in accordance with the Vedic scripture (*Maitrāyaṇīya Saṃhitā* 6.3.10.2): "Having cut off its head, they sprinkled it [with water] toward the cloud; it became the *prakṣa* tree. That is the nature of the *prakṣa*: that which is the branch of the *plakṣa*."

It is not the opinion of the Bhāṣyakāra— who derived the word *plakṣa* by adding the suffix *ac* (in the sense of the agent) to the root *kṣarati* preceded by the prefix *pra*, and then changing the *r* of the prefix to *l* on the grounds that *kapilaka* and others belong to the class of *ākṛtigaṇa* words (Pāṇini 6.1.157)— that such a derivation is valid; for otherwise, if the root *plakṣ* itself existed, the word *plakṣa* would be established simply by adding the suffix *ac* to that very root.

One should understand that this reading has been rejected in the *Mādhavadhātuvṛtti* after a thorough investigation based on the realization that the etymological derivation (*śrautanirvacana*) is not applicable here. The form *rephitvā* would result in two forms; however, Mādhava’s intention is that this is not so, because of the restrictive rule (*niyama*) adopted in [Pāṇini 1.2.23], *nopadhāt thaphāntād vā*, which implies "only from those with a non-*n* as penultimate. For the *kuṭādi* roots, the status of having the marker *ṅ* (*ṅittva*) is prescribed for suffixes other than those marked with *ñ* or *ṇ* (*ñit-ṇidbhinna*), in order to establish forms such as *kuṭitum* and *kuṭitā*. Likewise, in cases such as "even the Creator would lose his power to write" (*likhituṃ viśvasṛjo'pi śaktihāniḥ*) and "he will write by himself" (*svayameva likhiṣyate*), this is for the purpose of accounting for the absence of *guṇa* strengthening.

Regarding the rule *gāṅkuṭādibhyaḥ* (Pāṇini 1.2.1), some maintain that by expressing both a *bahuvrīhi* and a *tatpuruṣa* compound simultaneously—as in "the beginning of *kuṭa* is *kuṭādi*, and [the group] beginning with *kuṭa* is *kuṭādayaḥ*"—they accept that this root (*as*) also possesses the marker *ṅit*, since it is recited prior to *kuṭādi*. This position is refuted in the *Padamañjarī*; for otherwise, the grammatical indication in *apāccatuṣpācchakuniṣvālekhane* (6.1.142) and *ralo vyupadhāt* (1.2.26) would be inconsistent.

In this regard, since the examples *likhitvā* (having written), *lekhitvā* (having caused to write), *lilikhiṣati* (desires to write), and *lilekhiṣati* (desires to cause to write) are recorded in the *Kāśikā* and other works, and since the commentary (*vṛtti*) on the rule *īśvare tosun* (Pāṇini 3.4.13) explains it as "the meaning is *vilikhitum* (to write)," this position is not tenable. Vardhamāna and others have likewise stated this.

This is clear in the *Dhātuvṛtti* and other works. *Lubi* (1513), meaning "to crush" (*adarśane*), belongs to the *curādi* class (No. 1657). It is *akarmaka*, *seṭ*, and *ubhayapadī*. Deva states: "In the sense of crushing (*ardane*), one says *lumbayet* or *tumbayet*; with the suffix *śap*, [one says] *lumbati* or *tumbati*... (verse 139). In the *Kṣīrataraṅgiṇī*, it is stated as "—*ardane*. Deva and Maitreya read it simply as "*ardane*. Since the forms *lumbayati* and *lumbati* are established by the very fact of its inclusion in the *curādi* list and the addition of the *idit* marker, [the root is used] in the sense of crushing (*ardane*).

Its inclusion in the *bhvādi* class would be purposeless; however, since the meaning here in the *curādi* class is "not seeing," that inclusion in the *bhvādi* class becomes meaningful due to the difference in sense. Therefore, it appears that "in the sense of not seeing" alone is the correct reading.

→9. According to the rule *vā hatajagdhapareṣu* (Pāṇini 8.4.48), the doubling of the letter *t* in the word *putra* is optional when followed by the word *hata*.

→10. In the compound *kumārīhatā*, where it is a *karmadhāraya* meaning "a girl who has been killed," the vowel of the word *kumārī* is shortened according to the rule *gharūpakalpacelakṣbruvagotrahateṣu* (Pāṇini 6.3.43). Thus:
→1. By the rule "nadyāḥ śeṣasyānyatarasyām" (Pāṇini 6.3.44), there is an optional shortening of the vowel.
→2. However, by the prohibition "kṛnnadyāḥ pratiṣedhaḥ" (Vārttika on 6.3.44), the shortening does not occur because of that exception.

→ 4. Mādhava states that the *puṃvadbhāva* of the word *mahat* also applies here, according to the teaching of Ātreya.

According to the Vārttika on Pāṇini 3.1.97, *hano vā vadha ca*, when the suffix *yat* is applied in the sense of the object (*karman*), there is the substitution of *vadha* for the base form. When it functions as the object of the act of killing (*vadhakarmībhūta*), the suffix *ṇyat* is applied; with the substitution of *ku* and the change to *t*, the form is *ghātya*. And the substitution of *t* for *n* [is established]. Similarly, forms such as *bhrūṇahatyā* and others are also explained. Femininity [in these words] is due to their inherent nature (*svabhāvāt*).

→ 9. The word *aśvahatyā* is also established in the same manner as before: from the root *han*, with the suffix *kyap*, there is the substitution of *t* for the *n*. Mādhava states that some do not read this [rule].

→10. In this Vedic statement, it is clear from the *Mādhavīya* that the suffix *kyap* occurs even after the root *han* when it is used without an upapada, because of its archaic (*chāndasa*) character.

According to the rule “*hanter ghatvaṃ ca*” (Vārttika 6.1.12), when the root *han* takes the suffix *ac* (of the *pacādi* class), there is reduplication; the letter *gh* replaces the *h* in both the preceding and following syllables, and the augment *āk* is added to the preceding syllable. Thus, *ghanāghanaḥ* means “a rain-cloud” and also “a slayer. This is stated in the *Prakriyāsarvasva*: “*ghanāghanaḥ* = a rain-showering cloud, and a slayer. [As in: “*ghanāghanaḥ kṣobhaṇaś carṣaṇīnām*” (Taittirīya Saṃhitā 4.6.4.1).

→ 12. When the sense of a benediction (*āśis*) is implied—as in "may he slay the enemy"—the suffix *kṣa* is applied by the rule *āśiṣi hanaḥ* (Pāṇini 3.2.49), with "enemy" (*śatru*) as the object (*karman*). By the Vārttika rule *dārāvāhano’ṇ antasya ca ṭaḥ saṃjñāyām* (on Pāṇini 3.2.49), when the word *dāru* is the subordinate term (*upapada*), the suffix *aṇ* is applied [to the root *vah*], and the final letter of the stem is replaced by *ṭ*. From the root *han* preceded by the prefix *āṅ*, the suffix *aṇ* is applied in the sense of the agent (*kartari*), and the letter *n* is replaced by *ṭ* when forming a technical name (*saṃjñāyām*). → 1. One who strikes beautifully (*cāru*) is a *cārvāghāṭa*—or *cārvāghāta*. By the rule “*cārau vā*” (Vārttika on Pāṇini 3.2.49), the suffix *aṇ* is applied as before in the sense of the agent; there is an optional substitution of *ṭ* for the final letter, and because the suffix has the marker *ṇ*, the root vowel is replaced by *gh*. → 2. One who collects letters (*varṇān*) is a *varṇasaṃghāṭa* or *varṇasaṃghāta*. This is according to the rule “*karmaṇi sami ca*” (Vārttika on Pāṇini 3.2.49).
As before, [the suffix] *aṇ* and so forth apply.

Regarding the rule “*ape kleśatamasoḥ*” (Pāṇini 3.2.50), when *kleśa* and *tamas* are the accompanying words (*upapada*), the root *han* preceded by *apa* takes the suffix *kṣa*. Because it has the marker *kṣ*, there is the elision of the *ṭi* portion [of the root].

→4. Here, the suffix *kvip* is applied by the rule “*kvip ca*” (Pāṇini 3.2.76). When followed by a case-ending (*sup*), the vowel is lengthened by “*sau ca*” (6.4.13), and the *n* is elided. In the feminine, the suffix *ṅīp*—which would otherwise apply because the stem ends in *n* according to “*ṛnnebhyaḥ—*” (4.1.5)—does not occur;
for Mādhava states that the word “*han*” is included in the *gaṇa* list beginning with *bahu* (Gaṇasūtra 4.1.45) for the purpose of making the application of *ṅīṣ* optional.

This same derivation applies in cases such as *jvarāpahā* ("removing fever") and *niḥśeṣajāṅghyāpahā* ("removing all lameness"), and so forth. Kṣīrasvāmī, however, has established [the form] by means of the suffix *kṣa* according to the rule "also from others" (*anyebhyo 'pi*), just like *parikhā* and other examples.

In the case of the perfect tense (*liṭ*) with the suffix *kvasu*, there is optionally the augment *ikṣ* according to the rule "optionally for *gam*, *han*, *vid*, and *viś*" (*vibhāṣā gamahanavidaviśām*, Pāṇini 7.2.68).

In the case where the *iṭ* augment is present, the form is *jaghnivān*; in the case where the *iṭ* is absent, the form is *jaghanvān*. The substitution of *gh* for *han*, the elision of the penultimate vowel (*upadhā*), and so forth, should be understood as before.

Kṣīrasvāmī derives these forms by applying the suffix *kṣa* according to the rule "anyebhyo'pi—" (Pāṇini 3.2.178). Such a specific rule is not observed; rather, it appears that he intends to refer to a rule prescribing the suffix *kṣa* after the root *gam*.

It is called *varāha* because it digs up (*āhanti*) what is excellent (*vara*). It is called *paṭaha* because it is struck (*hanyate*) upon a cloth (*paṭa*). It is called *kalaha* because it destroys (*hanti*) sweetness (*kala*);

[here] the suffix *ghinuṇ* is applied in the sense of habitual action according to Pāṇini 3.2.142: "After the roots *sampṛc*, *āni*, *kṛ*, *vṛt*, *jñā*, *pū*, *mṛ*, and *muṣ*, and after *abhi* and *ā-han*."
And regarding the substitution of *ghatva* and *tatva*:

8. The suffix *ṇini* [is applied] by the rule "The suffix *ṇini* is used after the words *kumāra* and *śiras*" (Pāṇini 3.2.51). And there is the substitution of *ghatva* and *tatva*. Here, by virtue of this very irregular derivation (*nipātana*), the word *śiras* is replaced by *śīrṣa*. Furthermore, according to the statement "It should be stated that [the suffix applies] when [the agent] is contemptible" (Vārttika on 3.2.93), it is applied here.
The sense of reproach (*kutsā*) is to be illuminated.

→ 9. By the rule *lakṣaṇe jāyāpatyoṣṭak* (Pāṇini 3.2.52), the suffix *ṭak* is applied to the agent who possesses the characteristic (*lakṣaṇavat*). In the sūtra, the term "characteristic" (*lakṣaṇe*) refers by metonymy to that which possesses the characteristic. By the rule *gamahana-* (Pāṇini 6.4.98), there is elision of the penultimate vowel *a*. Then, the substitution of *gh* occurs.

A *jāyāghna* is one who possesses a particular kind of mole (*tilakālaka*). He is so called because there exists on his hands or other parts a mole in the shape of a *tila* that indicates the death of his wife. Similarly, a woman whose hand possesses a line indicative of killing her husband is called a *patighnī pāṇirekhā*. [This applies] in the case of the terms *jāyāghna* and *patighnī*.
The gender is determined by the force of the substantive (*viśeṣya*).

→ 1. By the rule "amanuṣyakartṛke ca" (Pāṇini 3.2.53), the suffix *ṭak* is applied. The grammatical derivation (*prakriyā*) is as before. Examples: *śleṣmaghnam madhu* (honey that destroys phlegm), *pittaghnaṃ jambīraphalam* (the citron fruit that destroys bile), *vātaghnaḥ śākaviśeṣaḥ* (a specific vegetable that destroys wind).

→ 2. In the sense of "one who kills a mouse," the suffix *aṇ* is applied by the rule *karmaṇyaṇ* (Pāṇini 3.2.1). Then, the substitution of *gh* for *h* and the subsequent change to *t* occur. → 3. Regarding this, some hold that the form is derived by adding the suffix *ka* according to the Vārttika *kaprakaraṇe mūlavibhujādibhyaḥ* (on Pāṇini 3.2.5), followed by the elision of the penultimate vowel (*upadhā*) and the substitution of *gh* for *h*. Mādhava, however, maintains that in the sense of "one who kills what has been made" (*kṛtaṃ hanti*), the suffix *lyuṭ* is applied by the rule *kṛtyalyuṭo bahulam* (Pāṇini 3.3.113).

Thus, by virtue of the inclusion of the term *bahulam* (in various ways) [in Pāṇini 3.3.113], he stated the suffix *ṭak*. In the same manner, the derivation applies to forms such as *kriyamāṇaghnaḥ*, *kariṣyamāṇaghnaḥ*, and *śatrughnaḥ*. With the suffix *ṭak*, there would be *kṛtaghnī* in the feminine; with the suffix *ka*, there would be *kṛtaghnā*.

→ 4. *Goghna* means "one for whom a cow is killed," i.e., a guest (*atithi*). By virtue of the rule "The suffix *ṭak* is applied after the roots *daṃś* and *han* when the recipient [is the object]" (Pāṇini 3.4.73), the suffix *ṭak* is applied in the sense of the recipient through specific grammatical derivation (*nipātana*). This word ends in a vowel (*ajanta*), according to the *Prakriyāsarvasva*.

→ 5. One who is capable of killing an elephant is expressed in this way. By the rule "The suffix *ṭak* is applied after the root *han* when 'capability' is meant, as well as with *hastin* and *kapāṭa*" (Pāṇini 3.2.54), the suffix *ṭak* is added to *han*.
An elephant-slayer is a soldier; a door-slayer is a thief. He who kills an elephant when [direct confrontation] is impossible by means of poison and the like is called an *hastighāta*.

Similarly, he who destroys a door-panel with many implements such as axes is called a *kapāṭaghāta*. In both cases, the suffix *aṇ* is applied according to Pāṇini 3.2.1 (*karmaṇyaṇ*). [The commentary notes: "In the case of *kavāṭa*s..."
There is a variation in the reading of the *sūtra*.

Regarding the form "pāṇigha": by virtue of the irregular derivation (*nipātana*) in Pāṇini 3.2.55, "In the sense of a craftsman, [the suffix] ṭak occurs after the roots han and akṣ," the suffix ṭak is applied to the root *han*, resulting in the elision of the final vowel (*ṭilopa*) and the substitution of *gh* for *h*. Thus, the form *pāṇighaḥ* is derived from "one who strikes with the hand" (*pāṇiṃ hanti*), referring to one who demonstrates proficiency in percussion instruments such as cymbals using only the hands.
*tākṣan* means "one who strikes the jaw" (*hanu*); thus *tākṣaghaḥ* refers to one who plays a specific musical instrument with the mouth alone.
→ 7. *pitṛvyaghātī* means "one who has killed his paternal uncle. According to Pāṇini 3.2.86, *karmaṇi hanaḥ*, the suffix *ṇini* is applied to the root *han* in the sense of the past action.

→ 8. From the root *han*, [the suffix] *kvip* is applied according to Pāṇini 3.2.87, *brahmabhrūṇavṛtreṣu kvip*. This applies only to the root *han*, and only when preceded by words such as *brahman* and others.

In this sūtra, there is a fourfold restriction: [the suffix] *kvip* occurs only after [roots ending in] *bhūta*. *brahmahā*: one who has killed a Brahmin. *bhrūṇahā*: one who has killed an embryo (*bhrūṇa* = *garbha*). *vṛtrahā*: Indra, who has killed Vṛtra. [The lengthening of the vowel occurs] by the rule *sau ca* (Pāṇini 6.4.13).
By accepting such a restriction, [the suffix] *kvip* is applied in cases such as *himahā*, *keśihā*, and *kālaneminihā*.
The suffix *kvip* is applied universally by the rule "ca" (Pāṇini 3.2.76).
This [form] ends in the second case plural (*dvitīyā-bahuvacana*). Here, there is an optional substitution of *ṇ* for *n* by the rule "prātipadikāntanumvibhaktiṣu ca" (8.2.154).

→10. By the rule "laṣapatapadasthābhūbṛṣahana—" (Pāṇini 3.2.154), the suffix *ukañ* is applied in the sense of habitual action (*tācchīlika*). Through the substitution of *gh* for *han*, and the subsequent change to *tat*, the feminine form is *ghātukī*.
→11. By the statement "bahulaṃ taṇyannavadhaka—" (Vārttika on Pāṇini 2.4.54), when the suffix *ṇvul* is applicable, the root *han* undergoes the substitution *vadha*.
Thus, this is a substitution ending in the vowel *a*. Alternatively, even though it ends in a consonant (*hal*), there is a prohibition of *vṛddhi* by the rule "janivadhyośca" (Pāṇini 7.3.15).
→ 1. By the rule "hanaśca vadhaḥ" (Pāṇini 3.3.76), when the suffix *ap* is added in the sense of an abstract action (*bhāva*), the root *han* undergoes the substitution *vadha*.

→ 2. According to the Vārttika on Pāṇini 3.3.58, "The suffix *ka* is prescribed in the sense of the suffix *ghañ* for the roots *sthā*, *snā*, *pā*, *vyadh*, *han*, and *yudh*," the suffix *kap* is applied. That which strikes (*hanti*) specifically is *vighna*.

→ 3. According to Pāṇini 3.3.77, "In the sense of a solid mass (*mūrti*), [the suffix] *ap* is added to *han*, and the root undergoes the substitution *ghana*"; this applies when hardness (*kāṭhinya*) is implied.

*Mūrti* means solidity (*kāṭhinyam*). *Abbhra-ghanaḥ* means the solidity of a cloud; *ghanaṃ dadhi* means solid curd. According to the *Prakriyāsarvasva*, the word *mūrti* is used to denote even an object qualified by its attributes. → 4. By the rule "antarghano deśe" (Pāṇini 3.3.78), when a location is to be expressed, [the form] is derived from this root preceded by *antar*.

When a suffix beginning with *ap-* follows, the root *han* undergoes the substitution of *ghan*. *Antarghanaḥ* is a specific village of the Vāhīkas; [the derivation is] "that in which one is struck (*hanyate*) within (*antar*)"—this is the function [of the rule]. Some read the form *antarghaṇaḥ*, with the substitution of *ṇ* already applied in the sūtra itself.

Their intention is that the substitution of *ṇ* is established by the statement: "It should be stated that the word *antar* functions as a preverb (*upasarga*) for the application of the augment *aṅ*, for the rules concerning *kit* and *ṇit* suffixes, and for the substitution of *ṇ*. (Vārttika on Pāṇini 1.4.65).

→ 5. [The forms] *praghaṇaḥ* and *praghāṇaḥ* are correct by virtue of the rule "agāraikadeśe praghaṇaḥ praghāṇaśca" (Pāṇini 3.3.79), which prescribes them as irregular forms (*nipātana*). When the external chamber or the porch (*alinda*) is to be expressed, the suffix *ap* is applied to the root *han* preceded by *pra*; in the form *praghāṇaḥ*, the substitution of *ghan* for the root and the lengthening of the vowel are obtained through this irregular prescription, as is the substitution of *ṇ*. In the form *praghaṇaḥ*, however, the substitution of *ṇ* is already established by the rule "hanteratpūrvasya" (Pāṇini 8.4.22).

→ 6. When *atyādhāna*—meaning that upon which another piece of wood or the like is placed and then carved—is intended [as the sense], the form is derived as before through the substitution of *ghana* and so forth, by virtue of the irregular derivation (*nipātana*) in the rule "udghano'tyādhānam" (Pāṇini 3.3.80).
→ 7. That which is struck away (*apa hanyate*) is correctly formed as *apaghana*, meaning "a limb," by virtue of the irregular derivation (*nipātana*) in the rule "apaghano'ṅgam" (Pāṇini 3.3.81).

→ 8. That by which iron is struck is *ayoghana*, meaning a hammer (*kūṭa*). That by which one is struck is *vighana*, meaning an instrument for leveling. That by which wood (*dru*) is struck is *drughana*, meaning an axe or similar tool. According to the rule "karaṇe'yovidruṣu" (Pāṇini 3.3.82), the suffix *ap* is added to the root *han* with the substitution of *ghana*. Some read it as *drughana*; in that case, [the ṇatva is justified] either by the rule "pūrvapadāt saṃjñāyāmagaḥ" (8.4.3) or because of the inclusion of "drughana" in the list of *arīhaṇa*-type words (4.2.80).

It should be understood that *ṇatva* does not apply here. → 9. When the word *stamba* is the *upapada*, the suffix *kap* is added to the root *han* in the sense of an instrument (*karaṇa*), and *ap* is also [added].

By the rule “*stambe ka ca*” (Pāṇini 3.3.83), when the suffix *kap* is applied, it becomes *stambaghnaḥ*; however, when the suffix *ap* is applied, it becomes *stambaghanaḥ*. Thus, an instrument such as a sickle is so called—that by which [one cuts].
A particular kind of grass (*stamba*) is struck down. The detailed explanation, however, is to be found in the *Mādhavīya*.

Regarding the rule "parau ghaḥ" (Pāṇini 3.3.84): when *pari* is the upapada, the suffix *ap* is added to the root *han*, and the suffix *gha* replaces the entire base (*prakṛti*). Thus, that which is struck around (*pari hanyate*) is a *parigha*—a bolt or bar. [This is further supported by] the rule "pareśca ghāṅkayoḥ."
(8-2-22) Thus, there is an option regarding the substitution of *l* for *r*. Consequently, the form *palighaḥ* also occurs.
Regarding the word *pratighaḥ*, Mādhava states that according to Ātreya, it is formed by the rule of diversity (*bāhulaka*). *Pratighaḥ* means anger.
[The form is derived] with the suffix *kṣa* by the rule "from others also" (3-2-101), and the change of *gh* to *g* occurs because the word belongs to the *nyakṣ-kvādi* group.
Bhānudīkṣita:

1. *Upaghna* means "nearby" (*pratyāsanna*). According to the rule *upaghna āśraye* (Pāṇini 3.3.85), there is a substitution by the suffix *ap* after the root *han*, with the elision of the penultimate vowel (*upadhā-lopa*). That which is approached (*upahanyate*) by means of a mountain is called *parvatopaghna*. In this case, the verbal root has the sense of "going."

→ 2. When the root *han* follows the prefixes *sam* or *ud*, and the suffix *ap* is applied provided that a "group" (*saṃgha*) or "praise" (*praśaṃsā*) is understood, the substitution of *gh* for *h* occurs by the rule *saṃghoddhau gaṇapraśaṃsayoḥ* (Pāṇini 3.3.86). *Saṃhananam* (the act of joining together) is a *saṃgha*—meaning a collection of living beings. The suffix *ap* is used here in the sense of an abstract state (*bhāva*). In other cases, it is *saṃghātaḥ*. *Uddhanyate* means "it is known as excellent"; since roots meaning "to go" (*gatyartha*) also carry the sense of "to know," *udghaḥ* means "praiseworthy. Here, the suffix *aṇ* is applied in the sense of an object (*karman*). In other cases, it is *udghātaḥ*.

→ 3. From this root preceded by the prefix *sam*, with the suffix *ghañ*, the word *saṃghāta* is correctly formed after the application of the rules for *ghatva* and *tatva*. Regarding this, Ātreya considers that the suffix *ghañ* here supersedes the suffixes *gha* and *ghañ*; whereas Mādhava states that the word *saṃghāta* is derived from the causative (*ṇijanta*) form, based on its inclusion in the list of roots beginning with *cura* under the rule “*hantyarthāśca*” (Gaṇasūtra, *curādi*).
→ 4. It is called *heti* because it strikes (*hanti*), or because one is struck by it (*hanyate’neneti*), according to the rule “*ūtiyūtijūtisātiheti—*” (Pāṇini 3.3.97).
According to Mādhava, the form *heti* is derived through the elision of *na* by means of a grammatical irregularity (*nipātana*), and the substitution of the vowel *i* for the radical vowel *a*.

The word *nigha* is correctly formed from this same root preceded by the prefix *ni*, with the suffix *ap*, based on the irregularity stated in Pāṇini 3.3.87: “*nigho nimittam*” (the word *nigha* denotes a cause).
*Nimitta* means measured all around; that is to say, it refers to the total height and circumference. [The term *nigha* is used] because things are struck down without distinction.
*Nighāḥ* refers to trees and rice plants.

*Nighnaḥ* means dependent or subordinate. From this root preceded by the prefix *ni*, the suffix *ka* is applied according to the rule "the application of *ka* in the sense of *ghañ*" (Vārttika on Pāṇini 3.3.58), due to the principle of diversity (*bāhulaka*).

→ 7. Regarding the rule *samūlākṛtajīveṣu han-* (Pāṇini 3.4.36), by the principle of correspondence (*yathāsaṃkhyam*), the suffix *ṇamul* is applied when *samūla* is the governing word (*upapada*). All its forms are to be understood like those of the root *kakhati* belonging to the *bhūvādigaṇa* (no. 142). Because it belongs to the *ghaṭādi* group, there is shortening of the vowel when the causative suffix *ṇic* is added.
